title: Swap Two Numbers
statement:
Given two integers A and B, swap their values and print them in the new order.

Input Format: A single line containing two space-separated integers A and B. | Output Format: A single line containing B followed by A, separated by a single space.

examples.explanation: After swapping, A becomes 5 and B becomes 3

title: Check Even or Odd
statement:
Given an integer N, check whether it is even or odd.

Input Format: A single line containing an integer N. | Output Format: Print Even if N is even, otherwise print Odd.

title: Print Numbers from 1 to N
statement:
Given an integer N, print all numbers from 1 to N in order.

Input Format: A single line containing an integer N. | Output Format: A single line with the numbers from 1 to N, separated by single spaces.

title: Calculate Sum of First N Natural Numbers
statement:
Given an integer N, calculate the sum of the first N natural numbers (1 + 2 + ... + N).

Input Format: A single line containing an integer N. | Output Format: A single integer, the sum of the first N natural numbers.

title: Print the Multiplication Table of a Number
statement:
Given a number N, print its multiplication table from 1 to 10.

Input Format: A single line containing an integer N. | Output Format: A single line with the products N x 1 to N x 10, separated by single spaces.

examples.explanation: 5 x 1 = 5, 5 x 2 = 10, and so on up to 5 x 10 = 50

title: Count Digits in a Number
statement:
Given a non-negative integer N, count how many digits it has.

Input Format: A single line containing a non-negative integer N. | Output Format: A single integer, the number of digits in N.

title: Find Sum of Array Elements
statement:
Given an array of N integers, find the sum of all its elements.

Input Format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers. | Output Format: A single integer, the sum of the array elements.

title: Find Smallest of Three Numbers
statement:
Given three integers A, B and C, find the smallest of the three.

Input Format: A single line containing three space-separated integers A, B and C. | Output Format: A single integer, the smallest of the three numbers.

title: Count Consonants in a String
statement:
Given a lowercase word with no spaces, count how many consonants it contains. Consonants are all letters except the vowels a, e, i, o, and u.

Input Format: A single line containing one lowercase word. | Output Format: A single integer representing the number of consonants.

title: Check Whether a String Contains Only Digits
statement:
Given a string, check whether it contains only digits (0-9).

Input Format: A single line containing a string with no spaces. | Output Format: Print Yes if every character is a digit, otherwise print No.

title: Reverse a String
statement:
Given a word with no spaces, print it in reverse.

Input Format: A single line containing one word. | Output Format: A single line with the reversed word.

title: Find Largest of Three Numbers
statement:
Given three integers A, B and C, find the largest of the three.

Input Format: A single line containing three space-separated integers A, B and C. | Output Format: A single integer, the largest of the three numbers.

title: Find Length of a String Without Built-in Functions
statement:
Given a word with no spaces, find its length by counting the characters one by one, without using any built-in length function.

Input Format: A single line containing one word. | Output Format: A single integer, the number of characters in the word.

title: Find Largest Element in an Array
statement:
Given an array of N integers, find the largest element in the array.

Input Format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers. | Output Format: A single integer, the largest element.

title: Find Smallest Element in an Array
statement:
Given an array of N integers, find the smallest element in the array.

Input Format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers. | Output Format: A single integer, the smallest element.

title: Sort an Array in Ascending Order
statement:
Given an array of N integers, sort it in ascending order.

Input Format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers. | Output Format: A single line with the sorted array elements, separated by single spaces.

title: Remove Duplicate Elements from an Array
statement:
Given an array of N integers, remove the duplicate elements and print the remaining elements in their original order, keeping the first occurrence of each value.

Input Format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers. | Output Format: A single line with the unique elements in their original order, separated by single spaces.

examples.explanation: Duplicates removed, first occurrence order kept

title: Find the Product of Digits of a Number
statement:
Given a non-negative integer N, find the product of its digits.

Input Format: A single line containing a non-negative integer N. | Output Format: A single integer, the product of the digits of N.

title: Find LCM of Two Numbers
statement:
Given two positive integers A and B, find their least common multiple (LCM), the smallest positive number divisible by both.

Input Format: A single line containing two space-separated integers A and B. | Output Format: A single integer, the LCM of A and B.

examples.explanation: 12 is the smallest number divisible by both 4 and 6

title: Check Whether a Number is a Strong Number
statement:
Given a positive integer N, check whether it is a Strong number. A Strong number equals the sum of the factorials of its digits (for example, 145 = 1! + 4! + 5! = 1 + 24 + 120).

Input Format: A single line containing a positive integer N. | Output Format: Print Yes if N is a Strong number, otherwise print No.

title: Count Vowels
statement:
Given a lowercase word with no spaces, count how many vowels it contains. The vowels are a , e , i , o , and u .

Input Format: A single line containing one lowercase word (1 ≤ length ≤ 1000). | Output Format: A single integer representing the number of vowels.

title: Prime Number Check
statement:
Given an integer n, print Yes if it is a prime number, otherwise print No . A prime number is greater than 1 and has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

Input Format: A single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1,000,000). | Output Format: Yes or No .

title: Second Largest Element
statement:
Given an array of n integers containing at least two distinct values, find and print the second largest distinct value in the array.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 1000). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: The second largest distinct integer.

title: Reverse a Number
statement:
Given a non-negative integer n, reverse its digits and print the resulting integer without any leading zeros.

Input Format: A single non-negative integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 10⁹). | Output Format: The reversed integer.

title: Factorial of a Number
statement:
Given a non-negative integer n, compute and print its factorial n!, where 0! = 1 and n! = 1 × 2 × ... × n.

Input Format: A single integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 20). | Output Format: A single integer representing n! (use a 64-bit integer type).

title: Count Even and Odd Numbers
statement:
Given an array of n integers, count how many elements are even and how many elements are odd. Note that 0 and negative multiples of 2 are even.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: Two space-separated integers: even_count odd_count .

title: Leap Year Check
statement:
Given a year y, print Yes if it is a leap year, otherwise print No . A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 400, or if it is divisible by 4 and not divisible by 100.

Input Format: A single integer y (1 ≤ y ≤ 10000). | Output Format: Yes or No .

title: Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)
statement:
Given two positive integers a and b, find and print their Greatest Common Divisor (the largest positive integer that divides both a and b without leaving a remainder).

Input Format: Two space-separated integers a and b (1 ≤ a, b ≤ 10⁹). | Output Format: A single integer representing GCD(a, b).

title: Armstrong Number Check
statement:
Given a positive integer n with d digits, print Yes if the sum of its digits each raised to the power d equals n; otherwise print No . For example, 153 = 1³ + 5³ + 3³.

Input Format: A single positive integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1,000,000). | Output Format: Yes or No .

title: Toggle Case of a String
statement:
Given a single word consisting only of uppercase and lowercase English letters, convert every uppercase letter to lowercase and every lowercase letter to uppercase, then print the resulting word.

Input Format: A single line containing one word (1 ≤ length ≤ 1000). | Output Format: The case-toggled word.

title: Find the Missing Number
statement:
Given an array containing n distinct integers taken from the range 0 to n , find and print the single number in that range that is missing from the array.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated distinct integers. | Output Format: The missing integer.

title: Valid Anagram
statement:
Given two lowercase English strings s and t, print True if t is an anagram of s (uses the exact same letters with the same frequencies), otherwise print False .

Input Format: Line 1: string s. Line 2: string t (1 ≤ length ≤ 5 × 10⁴). | Output Format: True or False .

title: Two Sum
statement:
Given an array of n integers and an integer target, find the two distinct 0-based indices i and j (i < j) such that nums[i] + nums[j] = target . Exactly one valid pair is guaranteed to exist.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers n and target (2 ≤ n ≤ 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: Two space-separated indices i j with i < j.

title: First Unique Character in a String
statement:
Given a lowercase English string s, find the first character that does not repeat anywhere else in the string and print its 0-based index. If every character repeats, print -1 .

Input Format: A single line containing lowercase string s (1 ≤ length ≤ 10⁵). | Output Format: An integer index or -1 .

title: Valid Parentheses
statement:
Given a string containing only the characters ( , ) , { , } , [ , and ] , print True if every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket in the correct order, otherwise print False .

Input Format: A single line string of brackets (1 ≤ length ≤ 10⁴). | Output Format: True or False .

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
statement:
Given an integer array sorted in non-decreasing order, remove duplicate elements so that each unique element appears only once while preserving the ascending order. Print the count of unique elements on the first line and the unique elements on the second line.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 3 × 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated sorted integers. | Output Format: Line 1: unique count k. Line 2: k space-separated unique integers.

title: Contains Duplicate
statement:
Given an integer array of length n, print True if any value appears at least twice in the array, and print False if every element is distinct.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: True or False .

title: Intersection of Two Arrays
statement:
Given two integer arrays, find all distinct elements that appear in both arrays and print them in ascending order separated by spaces. If the two arrays have no elements in common, print None .

Input Format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: m. Line 4: m space-separated integers (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 1000). | Output Format: Space-separated unique common integers in ascending order, or None .

title: Valid Palindrome (Alphanumeric)
statement:
Given a line of text that may contain letters, digits, spaces, and punctuation, convert all uppercase letters to lowercase and remove all non-alphanumeric characters. Print True if the resulting string reads the same forwards and backwards, otherwise print False .

Input Format: A single line string s (1 ≤ length ≤ 2 × 10⁴). | Output Format: True or False .

examples.input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

hiddenTestCases.input: Was it a car or a cat I saw?

title: Maximum Consecutive Ones
statement:
Given a binary array containing only 0 s and 1 s, find and print the maximum number of consecutive 1 s appearing in the array.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated binary integers ( 0 or 1 ). | Output Format: A single integer representing the longest streak of 1 s.

title: Sum of Digits
statement:
Given a non-negative integer n, find and print the sum of all its digits.

Input Format: A single non-negative integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 10⁹). | Output Format: A single integer representing the sum of its digits.

title: Palindrome Word
statement:
Given a single lowercase word with no spaces, print Yes if it reads the same forwards and backwards, otherwise print No .

Input Format: A single lowercase word (1 ≤ length ≤ 1000). | Output Format: Yes or No .

title: Fibonacci Sequence (First N Terms)
statement:
Given a positive integer n, print the first n terms of the Fibonacci sequence starting from 0 and 1 , where each subsequent term is the sum of the previous two terms.

Input Format: A single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 30). | Output Format: n space-separated integers.

title: Perfect Number Check
statement:
Given a positive integer n, print Yes if it is a perfect number, otherwise print No . A perfect number is equal to the sum of all its positive divisors excluding itself (for example, 6 = 1 + 2 + 3).

Input Format: A single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁶). | Output Format: Yes or No .

title: Decimal to Binary Conversion
statement:
Given a non-negative base-10 integer n, convert it into its binary (base-2) representation without unnecessary leading zeros.

Input Format: A single integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 10⁹). | Output Format: Binary string representing n.

title: Check if Array is Sorted
statement:
Given an array of n integers, print Yes if the array is sorted in non-decreasing order (each element is greater than or equal to the previous one), otherwise print No .

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: Yes or No .

title: Count Words in a Sentence
statement:
Given a single line of text containing words separated by one or more spaces (possibly with leading or trailing spaces), count and print the total number of words.

Input Format: A single line string s (1 ≤ length ≤ 1000). | Output Format: An integer representing the word count.

title: Frequency of a Target Element
statement:
Given an array of n integers and a target integer x, count and print how many times x appears in the array.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers n and x (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: A single integer representing the count of x.

title: Power of Two Check
statement:
Given an integer n, print Yes if there exists an integer k ≥ 0 such that n = 2ᵏ, otherwise print No .

Input Format: A single integer n (−10⁹ ≤ n ≤ 10⁹). | Output Format: Yes or No .

title: Matrix Row Sums
statement:
Given an r × c matrix of integers, calculate the sum of the elements in each row and print all row sums on a single line separated by spaces.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers r and c (1 ≤ r, c ≤ 100). Next r lines: c space-separated integers each. | Output Format: r space-separated integers.

title: Roman to Integer
statement:
Roman numerals use seven symbols: I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000 . A smaller symbol placed before a larger symbol indicates subtraction (e.g., IV=4, IX=9, XL=40, XC=90, CD=400, CM=900 ). Given a valid Roman numeral in the range 1 to 3999, convert it to an integer.

Input Format: A single uppercase Roman numeral string. | Output Format: The corresponding integer value.

title: Majority Element
statement:
Given an array of n integers, find and print the majority element — the element that appears strictly more than ⌊n / 2⌋ times. You may assume a majority element always exists. Aim for O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 5 × 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: The majority integer.

title: Longest Common Prefix
statement:
Given an array of n lowercase English words, find the longest common prefix string shared by all of them. If there is no common prefix, print NONE .

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 200). Line 2: n space-separated lowercase words. | Output Format: The longest common prefix, or NONE .

title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
statement:
Given two arrays of integers already sorted in non-decreasing order, merge them into a single sorted array and print all n + m elements. Aim for O(n + m) time using two pointers rather than re-sorting.

Input Format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: m. Line 4: m sorted integers (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 5 × 10⁴). | Output Format: n + m space-separated sorted integers.

title: Isomorphic Strings
statement:
Given two strings s and t of equal length, print True if they are isomorphic, otherwise print False . Two strings are isomorphic if the characters in s can be replaced consistently to form t, where no two different characters may map to the same character.

Input Format: Line 1: string s. Line 2: string t (1 ≤ length ≤ 5 × 10⁴). | Output Format: True or False .

title: Is Subsequence
statement:
Given two lowercase strings s and t, print True if s is a subsequence of t, otherwise print False . A subsequence is formed from t by deleting zero or more characters without changing the relative order of the remaining characters.

Input Format: Line 1: string s. Line 2: string t (1 ≤ length ≤ 10⁴). | Output Format: True or False .

title: Binary Search
statement:
Given an array of n distinct integers sorted in ascending order and a target value, find and print the 0-based index of target if it exists in the array; otherwise print -1 . Implement an O(log n) solution.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers n and target (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated sorted integers. | Output Format: The 0-based index or -1 .

title: Find Pivot Index
statement:
Given an array of n integers, find the leftmost 0-based pivot index where the sum of all elements strictly to its left equals the sum of all elements strictly to its right. If the index is on the left or right edge, the empty side has a sum of 0 . Print -1 if no pivot index exists.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: Leftmost pivot index or -1 .

title: Excel Sheet Column Number
statement:
Given a string representing an Excel spreadsheet column title using uppercase English letters ( A → 1, B → 2, ..., Z → 26, AA → 27, AB → 28 ), compute and print its corresponding positive column number.

Input Format: A single uppercase string (1 ≤ length ≤ 6). | Output Format: The integer column number.

title: Climb Stairs
statement:
You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each time you can climb either 1 step or 2 steps. Find and print the total number of distinct ways you can reach the top.

Input Format: A single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 45). | Output Format: A single integer representing the number of distinct ways.

title: Single Number
statement:
Given a non-empty array of n integers where every element appears exactly twice except for one element that appears once, find and print that single element. Aim for O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

Input Format: Line 1: odd integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 3 × 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: The single unique integer.

title: Plus One
statement:
You are given a large non-negative integer represented as an array of n digits ordered from most significant to least significant (no leading zeros except for 0 itself). Increment the integer by one and print the resulting digits separated by spaces.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100). Line 2: n space-separated digits (0–9). | Output Format: Space-separated digits of the incremented integer.

title: Length of Last Word
statement:
Given a string s consisting of words and spaces (which may include trailing spaces), find and print the length of the last word in the string. A word is a maximal sequence of non-space characters.

Input Format: A single line string s (1 ≤ length ≤ 10⁴). | Output Format: An integer representing the length of the last word.

title: Monotonic Array
statement:
An array is monotonic if it is either entirely non-decreasing (nums[i] ≤ nums[i+1]) or entirely non-increasing (nums[i] ≥ nums[i+1]). Given an array of n integers, print True if it is monotonic, otherwise print False .

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: True or False .

title: Reverse Words in a String
statement:
Given a line of text containing words separated by one or more spaces (possibly with leading or trailing spaces), reverse the order of the words and print them separated by a single space with no leading or trailing spaces.

Input Format: A single line string s (1 ≤ length ≤ 10⁴). | Output Format: The words in reversed order, single-space separated.

title: Move Zeroes
statement:
Given an array of n integers, move all 0 s to the end of the array while maintaining the relative order of all non-zero elements. Implement this in-place without creating a copy of the array.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: n space-separated integers after moving zeroes.

title: Search Insert Position
statement:
Given a sorted array of n distinct integers and a target value, print the 0-based index if the target is found. If not, print the 0-based index where it would be inserted to keep the array sorted. Implement an O(log n) solution.

Input Format: Line 1: integers n and target (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁴). Line 2: n strictly increasing integers. | Output Format: The target or insertion index.

title: Two Sum II (Sorted Array)
statement:
Given a 1-indexed array of n integers sorted in non-decreasing order and a target integer, find the two distinct 1-based indices i and j (1 ≤ i < j ≤ n) such that nums[i] + nums[j] = target . Solve in O(n) time and O(1) extra space using two pointers.

Input Format: Line 1: integers n and target (2 ≤ n ≤ 3 × 10⁴). Line 2: n sorted integers. | Output Format: Two space-separated 1-based indices i j .

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement:
Given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i, choose a single day to buy one share and a later day to sell it to maximize profit. Print the maximum profit achievable, or 0 if no profit is possible.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated non-negative integers. | Output Format: Maximum profit integer.

title: Find the Duplicate Number
statement:
Given an array of n integers where every number lies in the range 1 to n − 1 and exactly one integer is repeated (two or more times), find and print the repeated integer. Follow-up: solve in O(n) time and O(1) extra space without modifying the array.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated integers in [1, n − 1]. | Output Format: The duplicate integer.

title: Rotate Array
statement:
Given an integer array of length n and a non-negative integer k, rotate the array to the right by k steps and print the resulting array. Note that k may be larger than n. Aim for O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵, 0 ≤ k ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: n space-separated integers after rotation.

title: Sort Colors
statement:
Given an array of n integers containing only 0 s, 1 s, and 2 s, sort the array in-place so that elements of the same value are adjacent in the order 0 , 1 , 2 . You must not use a built-in sorting function.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated integers (each 0, 1, or 2). | Output Format: n space-separated sorted integers.

title: Find First and Last Position in Sorted Array
statement:
Given an array of n integers sorted in non-decreasing order and a target value, find the starting and ending 0-based indices of target in the array. If target is not found, print -1 -1 . Implement an O(log n) binary search solution.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers n and target (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated sorted integers. | Output Format: Two space-separated integers first last .

title: Jump Game
statement:
You are given an array of n non-negative integers where each element represents the maximum jump length from that index. Starting at index 0 , print True if you can reach the last index ( n − 1 ), otherwise print False .

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated non-negative integers. | Output Format: True or False .

title: Spiral Matrix Traversal
statement:
Given an r × c matrix of integers, print all elements of the matrix in clockwise spiral order starting from the top-left corner, separated by single spaces on one line.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers r and c (1 ≤ r, c ≤ 50). Next r lines: c space-separated integers each. | Output Format: r × c space-separated integers in spiral order.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
statement:
Given an array of n integers (which may contain negative numbers and zeros) and an integer k, find and print the total number of non-empty contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k. Aim for an O(n) prefix-sum hash map solution.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 2 × 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: Total count of valid subarrays.

title: Container With Most Water
statement:
You are given an array height of n non-negative integers where each value represents the height of a vertical line drawn at x-coordinate i. Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the maximum possible amount of water, and print that maximum area. Aim for an O(n) two-pointer solution.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated non-negative integers. | Output Format: Maximum water area integer.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement:
Given an unsorted array of n integers, find and print the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers (for example, 1, 2, 3, 4 ). Duplicate elements do not extend the sequence. Implement an O(n) algorithm using a hash set.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: Length of the longest consecutive sequence.

title: Daily Temperatures
statement:
Given an array of n daily temperatures, for each day i compute how many days you must wait until a strictly warmer temperature occurs. If there is no future day with a warmer temperature, output 0 for that day. Aim for an O(n) monotonic stack solution.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: n space-separated wait-day counts.

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
statement:
Given an array of n positive integers and a positive integer target, find and print the minimal length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is greater than or equal to target. If no such subarray exists, print 0 . Aim for an O(n) sliding window solution.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers n and target (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵, 1 ≤ target ≤ 10⁹). Line 2: n space-separated positive integers. | Output Format: Minimal subarray length or 0 .

title: Product of Array Except Self
statement:
Given an integer array nums of length n, compute an array answer such that answer[i] equals the product of all elements of nums except nums[i]. You must solve it in O(n) time without using the division operator.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: n space-separated integers.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement:
Given a string s containing lowercase English letters, find and print the length of the longest contiguous substring that contains no repeating characters. Aim for an O(n) sliding window solution.

Input Format: A single line string s (1 ≤ length ≤ 5 × 10⁴). | Output Format: Integer length of the longest unique-character substring.

title: 3Sum
statement:
Given an integer array of length n, find all unique triplets a b c (from three distinct indices) such that a + b + c = 0. Print each triplet in non-decreasing order ( a ≤ b ≤ c ), and print all unique triplets sorted lexicographically, one per line. If no valid triplet exists, print NONE .

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 3000). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: Sorted unique triplets one per line, or NONE .

title: House Robber
statement:
You are given an array of n non-negative integers representing the amount of money stored in each house along a street. Adjacent houses have connected security systems, so you cannot rob two adjacent houses. Find and print the maximum total money you can rob without triggering the alarm.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated non-negative integers. | Output Format: Maximum rob amount integer.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
statement:
Given an integer array of length n (which may contain negative numbers and zeros), find the contiguous non-empty subarray that has the largest product and print that maximum product.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2 × 10⁴). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: Maximum product integer.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement:
An integer array of n distinct elements sorted in ascending order has been rotated at an unknown pivot index. Given the rotated array and a target value, print the 0-based index of target if it exists, otherwise print -1 . You must implement an O(log n) binary search algorithm.

Input Format: Line 1: two integers n and target (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: 0-based index or -1 .

title: Number of Islands
statement:
Given an m × n 2D grid of 1 s (land) and 0 s (water), count and print the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and formed by connecting adjacent land cells horizontally or vertically (not diagonally).

Input Format: Line 1: two integers m and n (1 ≤ m, n ≤ 300). Next m lines: a string of n characters ( 0 or 1 ). | Output Format: Total number of islands.

title: Word Break
statement:
Given a lowercase string s and a dictionary of k words, print True if s can be segmented into a sequence of one or more dictionary words (dictionary words may be reused any number of times), otherwise print False .

Input Format: Line 1: string s (1 ≤ length ≤ 300). Line 2: integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ 1000). Line 3: k space-separated dictionary words. | Output Format: True or False .

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement:
Given an integer array of length n, find and print the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. A subsequence is formed by deleting zero or more elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.

Input Format: Line 1: integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2500). Line 2: n space-separated integers. | Output Format: Integer length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

title: Course Schedule
statement:
There are numCourses courses labeled from 0 to numCourses − 1 and m prerequisite pairs. Each pair a b indicates that you must finish course b before taking course a. Print True if it is possible to finish all courses, otherwise print False .

Input Format: Line 1: two integers numCourses and m (1 ≤ numCourses ≤ 2000, 0 ≤ m ≤ 5000). Next m lines: two integers a b. | Output Format: True or False .
